name: Phillip T. (Terry) Ragon
current_role: Founder, CEO and sole owner, InterSystems Corporation (Cambridge, MA)
profile: Terry Ragon, an MIT physics graduate, founded data-platform software company InterSystems in 1978; it still is wholly owned by him and has around $1B in annual sales, serving hospitals, banks and government health systems. With his wife Susan he funds the Ragon Institute of MGH, MIT and Harvard, endowed with a $200M gift in 2019, which works on HIV and other vaccines.
interesting_fact: After a 2009 trip to South Africa where they saw the toll of AIDS, Terry and Susan Ragon set up the Ragon Institute to pursue an HIV vaccine; they joined the Giving Pledge in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He got his first programming job at Meditech, an early electronic medical records company, after admitting in the interview, 'I really don't know much about computers... But I play guitar.' There he learned MUMPS, the hospital programming language InterSystems was later built on.
notes: Very low-profile; rarely gives interviews (the 2024 Forbes piece was described as a rare one). Best route is InterSystems PR. The Ragon Institute (ragoninstitute.org) is another angle.

name: Maha Vajiralongkorn Phra Vajiraklaochaoyuhua
profile: Vajiralongkorn is the reigning King of Thailand, the only son of King Bhumibol Adulyadej; he took the throne in 2016 and was crowned in 2019. Hurun counts his wealth through his holdings in Siam Commercial Bank, assets once managed by the Crown Property Bureau that he took into direct ownership after his accession.
interesting_fact: He is a graduate of Australia's Royal Military College, Duntroon, and qualified as both a military fast-jet pilot and a commercial airline pilot.
deep_cut_fact: He was once known as the 'Football Prince': he played forward and later centre-back at Chitralada School, Millfield School in Somerset and Duntroon. Since 1978 he has personally handed out degrees at Rajabhat University commencements every year, estimated at over 2.1 million degrees.
notes: Reigning monarch, not a realistic podcast guest. Thailand's strict lese-majeste laws make any outreach or commentary sensitive. The only channel is formal, via the Bureau of the Royal Household. No personal contacts are published.

name: Wu Yan
current_role: Co-owner with husband Wang Qicheng of the Hakim Unique (汉鼎宇佑) group's holdings; former controlling shareholder of Hakim Unique (300300.SZ, now 海峡创新)
profile: Hurun's Wu Yan (吴艳) is listed jointly with her husband Wang Qicheng, founder of Hangzhou-based Hakim Unique Group (汉鼎宇佑), a conglomerate with more than 150 companies. In 2019 she sold a 15% stake and control of listed Hakim Unique to state-linked Pingtan Chuangtou for RMB 1.05B. Wang now invests through platforms such as Qianshan Capital.
interesting_fact: The couple were ranked No. 5 on Hurun's 2019 list of self-made rich people born in the 1980s, with RMB 18B; Wang was once the youngest controlling shareholder of an A-share company, at 31.
notes: The input's SEC link (Microvast CEO) is a name collision. Microvast's CEO is Yang Wu, a different person, so ignore it. Wu Yan has almost no public profile of her own and the details are mostly about her husband. Identity is marked uncertain on the person level; the source of wealth ('Hakim' = 汉鼎宇佑) matches. No published contacts found.

name: Kwon Hyuk-bin
current_role: Founder and Chief Vision Officer (CVO), Smilegate Holdings; chairman of Smilegate Hope Studio foundation
profile: Kwon founded Smilegate in 2002 and owns it outright. A 2008 publishing deal with Tencent turned its shooter CrossFire into a global hit in China, and the later MMORPG Lost Ark followed. Smilegate is among Korea's largest game companies. He became CVO in 2020 and backs startups through the Orange Planet Entrepreneurship Foundation and charity work through Smilegate Hope Studio.
interesting_fact: In 2020 he became the first person from Korea's game industry to receive a national Order of Cultural Merit (cultural medal).
deep_cut_fact: Smilegate's very first game was not CrossFire but an FPS called Headshot Online, finished around 2005. Its official launch was cancelled when the publisher, Yahoo Korea, left the games business. As a student he took part in Samsung's Software Membership developer program.
notes: Rarely speaks publicly. His 2026 divorce litigation, which affects Smilegate's ownership, is in the news; avoid it. Orange Planet, the startup foundation, is a natural entrepreneurship angle for a podcast. The Samsung Software Membership fact is from the Forbes facts and a Wikipedia mirror.

name: Joe Lonsdale
current_role: Managing Partner, 8VC (Austin, TX); host of the American Optimist podcast
profile: Joe Lonsdale co-founded Palantir in 2004, then wealth-data platform Addepar (2009) and government software firm OpenGov, and started VC firm 8VC in 2015, which he moved to Austin in 2020. 8VC has about $6B in assets, with bets in defense tech, logistics and life sciences. He also founded the Cicero Institute policy think tank and co-founded the University of Austin.
interesting_fact: He began his career at Peter Thiel's hedge fund Clarium Capital straight out of Stanford, after interning at PayPal, and then helped build Palantir's first prototype in 2004.
deep_cut_fact: Before Palantir, he was editor-in-chief of The Stanford Review in 2002–03. It is the student paper Peter Thiel co-founded in 1987, the link that led to his PayPal internship and Clarium job.
notes: Very accessible and media-friendly: hosts his own podcast and posts a lot on X. Interested in energy and data-center policy. Best routes are press@8vc.com or X.

name: Fabrizio Di Amato
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, MAIRE S.p.A. (Rome/Milan); Chairman, Maire Foundation
profile: Rome-born Di Amato started his business at 19 with three employees. Through acquisitions including Fiat Engineering (2004), Tecnimont (2005), Stamicarbon (2009) and KT (2010) he built MAIRE, now an energy-transition engineering and technology group with 9,800+ staff in 45 countries. He listed it in Milan in 2007, and in 2018 he founded NextChem, its sustainable-technology arm working on hydrogen, ammonia, SAF and circular chemistry.
interesting_fact: In 2008 he founded Federprogetti, the Italian Plant Engineering Federation, and chaired it until 2015. He was made a Cavaliere del Lavoro (Knight of Labour) in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: His degree is in Political Science from La Sapienza, yet the Politecnico di Milano later gave him an honorary degree in Chemical Engineering. His Maire Foundation preserves the group's historic engineering archives and trains 'humanist engineers' for the energy and digital transitions.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast: MAIRE/NextChem work on hydrogen, ammonia, SAF and nuclear MoUs (e.g. Nuward). The group media relations contact named in releases is Tommaso Verani. The press-release contact block was confirmed via search snippet, not opened directly.

name: Ted Turner
notes: Died May 6, 2026, aged 87 (AP). Source: https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/may/6/ted-turner-cnn-founder-brash-outspoken-television-pioneer-died-age-87/. Rest skipped per instructions.

name: Jami Gertz
current_role: Co-owner, Atlanta Hawks (with husband Tony Ressler); actress; philanthropist (Ressler-Gertz Foundation)
profile: Jami Gertz is the actress known for The Lost Boys, Less than Zero, Twister and the CBS sitcom Still Standing. Her listed fortune is shared with her husband Tony Ressler, co-founder of Ares Management. Their group bought majority control of the NBA's Atlanta Hawks in 2015 for about $730M, and the couple give through the Ressler-Gertz Foundation to education, Los Angeles and Jewish causes.
interesting_fact: She was discovered by Norman Lear in a nationwide talent search and reportedly turned down the role of Rachel Green on Friends during pre-production.
deep_cut_fact: Between acting jobs she worked in Paris as a scent designer for the fashion house Lanvin. She grew up in Glenview, Illinois, and graduated from Maine East High School.
notes: Private; rarely appears in public. Wealth is through Tony Ressler (Ares Management), who is the better entrepreneurship or podcast angle. No personal or foundation contact was published; the Atlanta Hawks communications office is the institutional route. Gertz is also a Melanoma Research Alliance board member.

name: Qian Dongqi
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Ecovacs Robotics (科沃斯, 603486.SH), Suzhou
profile: Qian Dongqi (b. 1958), a Nanjing University physics graduate with a master's in philosophy, worked in state-owned foreign trade before renting a village factory in Suzhou in 1998 to start Taiyikai Electric, an OEM vacuum maker. It became Ecovacs, one of China's largest robot-vacuum brands, and listed in Shanghai in 2018. The group also owns Tineco, the floor-cleaner brand run by his son David Qian.
interesting_fact: Before launching its own brands, the company made vacuums for other labels; by around 2006 this OEM business already brought in about RMB 1B a year.
deep_cut_fact: The idea for a robot vacuum reportedly came from a 1999/2000 news story about a robot soccer match, which made Qian wonder whether a robot could sweep floors. The company kept the name Taiyikai (泰怡凯) until 2011.
notes: The email is the general contact in the Ecovacs Group website's site config, not a named press office. For IR, use the SSE disclosures for 603486. The sources disagree on the year of the robot-soccer anecdote (1999 vs 2000). David Qian, chairman of Tineco, is the more media-facing family member.

name: Fernando Roig
current_role: President and majority owner, Villarreal CF; owner and president, Pamesa Cerámica; ~9% shareholder in Mercadona
profile: Fernando Roig Alfonso (b. 1947), brother of Mercadona chief Juan Roig, helped his siblings take over their parents' eight-store grocery in 1981 and keeps about 9% of Mercadona. He owns ceramic-tile maker Pamesa (Almazora, Castellón) and bought control of Villarreal CF in 1997–98 while it was in the Segunda División. He built it into a regular in European competition and La Liga.
interesting_fact: Roig bought Villarreal while it was a second-division club; under him it reached La Liga and played in the UEFA Cup and the Champions League. Spanish Wikipedia also says he has wind-energy interests through the company Renomar.
deep_cut_fact: In January 2017 Villarreal renamed its century-old El Madrigal ground 'Estadio de la Cerámica' in tribute to the local ceramics industry, the business behind Roig's Pamesa. Vila-real named him its 'Hijo Adoptivo' (adopted son) in 2006.
notes: No press email was found for Villarreal or Pamesa; the club contact page lists only ticketing, shop and GDPR addresses. His wind-energy holding Renomar (renomar.es) could be an energy angle, but its link to Roig is sourced only from Spanish Wikipedia.

notes: Oil industrialist (Davis Petroleum; former owner of 20th Century Fox, Pebble Beach, Beverly Hills Hotel). Died September 25, 2004; he is on the Forbes 1997–98 lists. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvin_Davis. Rest skipped per instructions.

name: Hans Georg Naeder
current_role: Chairman of the Board (Verwaltungsrat) / Chairman of the Management Board, Ottobock SE & Co. KGaA; majority owner via Näder Holding
profile: Hans Georg Näder (b. 1961, Duderstadt) is the third-generation head of Ottobock, the prosthetics and orthotics maker founded by his grandfather Otto Bock in 1919. He took over from his father in 1990 at age 28 and built it into a world leader with over 10,000 staff and 60 country branches. Ottobock listed in Frankfurt in October 2025; his family holding keeps roughly 80% of the shares.
interesting_fact: Ottobock has given on-site technical repair service at every Paralympic Games since Seoul 1988, became the IPC's first Worldwide Partner in 2005, and is signed on through Brisbane 2032.
deep_cut_fact: He has been an honorary professor at PFH Göttingen since 2005 and pushed for its new 'Orthobionik' (orthobionics) degree course. He has also been a guest professor at Capital Medical University in Beijing since 2009.
notes: Press contact is Merle Florstedt, Head of Corporate Communications, as named in Ottobock press releases. Avoid the pending VAT investigation over yacht purchases and the May 2026 short-seller report. He is a keen sailor (yacht Pink Gin won the 2007 Millennium Cup per Forbes), but no independent source was confirmed for that.

name: Hiroshi Ishibashi
current_role: Chairman, Ishibashi Foundation; Director, Artizon Museum (Tokyo); Chairman, AXIS Inc.
profile: Hiroshi Ishibashi (石橋寛, b. 1946, Fukuoka) is a grandson of Bridgestone founder Shojiro Ishibashi and holds a small but valuable Bridgestone stake, with no executive role. He chairs the Ishibashi Foundation, which in 2020 rebuilt the Bridgestone Museum of Art and reopened it as the Artizon Museum in central Tokyo.
interesting_fact: The museum's new name, Artizon, blends 'ART' and 'HORIZON'. Its collection runs from Impressionism to contemporary art and design, including furniture by Shiro Kuramata and Ettore Sottsass.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a car and industrial designer at Art Center College of Design in Los Angeles from 1964, set up Bridgestone's in-house design department and corporate identity, and in 1981 founded AXIS, the Roppongi design hub and magazine, opening with a Sottsass show. He won the Red Dot 'Personality' award in 2023.
notes: Best route is via the Artizon Museum or Ishibashi Foundation press office; no press email was readable in the PDFs. The AXIS design-entrepreneur story is a good conversation angle.

name: Rishad Naoroji
current_role: Founder, Raptor Research and Conservation Foundation (Mumbai); member, Governing Council, Bombay Natural History Society
profile: Rishad Naoroji (b. 1951) is a Godrej family member and cousin of Adi, Nadir and Jamshyd Godrej. His fortune comes from a one-fifth share of the family's assets, though he never worked in the business; after the 2024 split of the Godrej group, filings show he sold his stakes to his cousins. He is a raptor biologist, wildlife photographer and author.
interesting_fact: He wrote 'Birds of Prey of the Indian Subcontinent' (2006/07), described as the first species-by-species book on the region's raptors, covering all 69 resident and migrant species. A reviewer said it seemed about 25 years in the making.
deep_cut_fact: He has published field ornithology himself, for example 'Breeding of the Red-headed Falcon Falco chicquera in Saurashtra, Gujarat' in Forktail (2011). His own 1992 photo of a female Mountain Hawk-Eagle on its nest in Corbett Tiger Reserve appears in his book.
notes: Very low-profile and not a business figure. A conservation or birding angle is the only natural hook. No published contact was found; the Bombay Natural History Society (bnhs.org) is a possible institutional route.

name: Luis Enrique Yarur Rey
current_role: Board member, Banco de Crédito e Inversiones (BCI), City National Bank of Florida and Empresas JY; Chairman, Empresas Jordan and MAS Analytics. He chaired BCI 1991–2024.
profile: A lawyer by training, Yarur joined family-founded BCI in 1975, served 11 years as general manager and chaired it from 1991 until stepping down on 31 Dec 2024; his son Ignacio succeeded him. Under him, BCI expanded into Florida with City National Bank (2015), TotalBank and Executive National Bank, and reportedly grew profits 58-fold. He pushed a decade-long digital transformation.
interesting_fact: In 1994 he and his brothers took control of BCI by buying a 34% stake from their uncle Jorge Yarur Banna's estate. BCI's 2015 purchase of City National Bank of Florida was the first acquisition of a US bank by a Chilean bank.
deep_cut_fact: Even after leaving the BCI chair he kept the chairmanship of MAS Analytics, a Chilean data-analytics and AI consultancy. He also sits on the boards of Fundación Enseña Chile (Teach for Chile) and Chile Mujeres.
notes: No longer BCI chairman (since Jan 2025); the Forbes bio is out of date. MAS Analytics (masanalytics.cl) is a data/AI angle for the podcast. No press email was found on BCI pages fetched by script.

name: Liang Feng
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Executive Director, Shanghai Putailai New Energy Technology (璞泰来, 603659.SH); controlling shareholder of Puyuan Materials (璞源材料, 603196.SH, formerly Ribo Fashion)
profile: Liang Feng (b. 1968), an automation engineer with an economics master's from Zhejiang University, co-founded Putailai with Chen Wei in 2012. It supplies anode materials, separator coating and lithium-battery production equipment to makers such as CATL, Samsung and LG. It listed in Shanghai in 2017 and filed for a Hong Kong secondary listing in March 2026. In 2023 he took control of listed Ribo Fashion, now Puyuan Materials.
interesting_fact: Putailai crossed RMB 1B in revenue within four years of its 2012 founding. CATL accounts for nearly 40% of its revenue.
deep_cut_fact: Before batteries he was a public fund manager, at China AMC (华夏基金) in 2005–07 and AIG-Huatai (now Huatai-PineBridge) in 2007–10. He started his career in 1990 as an engineering group manager at SAE Magnetics' Dongguan plant (东莞新科磁电), where he met co-founder Chen Wei.
notes: A battery supply-chain founder, relevant for an energy and storage angle. The board secretary is Zhang Xiaoquan, per 2026 disclosures. The IR email is confirmed via search snippet of the 2026 annual-report disclosure.
